meta.title: win-translate — one translation, end to end

messages.label: press Ctrl+Alt+T
messages.note: RegisterHotKey reports only this one combination. A keyboard hook would see every keystroke typed, including passwords.

messages.label: release held modifiers, then Ctrl+C
messages.note: Ctrl+Alt is still physically down. Without releasing it first the app receives Ctrl+Alt+C, which is not a copy.

messages.label: poll GetClipboardSequenceNumber
messages.note: Copying is asynchronous. A fixed sleep truncates on a slow app and wastes time on a fast one.

messages.label: put the old contents back
messages.note: Only text survives the round trip. An image or a file list on the clipboard is cleared rather than restored.

messages.label: captured signal (queued)
messages.note: Crosses to the Qt thread. Every widget touch happens here and nowhere else.

messages.label: one thread per request
messages.note: The HTTP call sits on a third thread so a slow network cannot freeze the popup that is already on screen.

messages.label: HTTP 429
messages.note: Measured, not assumed: translate.googleapis.com is throttled from some networks while clients5 answers normally.

messages.label: translation + detected language
messages.note: If the detected language is already the target, it asks again in the other direction. Only the reverse direction costs two requests.

messages.label: translated signal (queued)
messages.note: Carries the request_id. A slower earlier request is discarded; only the newest one is painted.

cards.title: Three threads, and why
items: The hotkey thread captures the selection in place, because it has to happen while the other app still owns the foreground
The Qt main thread owns every widget — the popup is touched from here and nowhere else
The worker thread holds the HTTP call, so a slow network cannot freeze a popup that is already on screen

cards.title: Why it borrows the clipboard
items: Windows has no API to ask another process what it has selected
UI Automation's TextPattern answers for some controls, but Chrome and Electron do not expose it reliably
So: save the clipboard, synthesise Ctrl+C, wait for the sequence number to move, read, put it back

cards.title: What differs on macOS
items: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey delivers through the Qt event loop, so there are TWO threads here, not three
Cmd+C is sent again when the first copy goes unanswered, and the whole path needs Accessibility permission
A real right-click entry is only reachable on this side, through NSServices — still not built
